summary:
Traditional Medicare Part B (CGS J15 for Kentucky, WPS J8 for Indiana) runs on federal law only. Kentucky and Indiana prompt-pay statutes and insurance-department complaints do not reach a MAC, and nothing in 42 CFR 405 Subpart I or SSA 1869 gives damages, bad-faith remedies or deemed approval.

DO THEY HAVE TO ANSWER, AND BY WHEN? Yes, on fixed clocks:
- Clean claims: paid within 30 days of receipt, or Medicare adds interest on its own at the Treasury Prompt Payment rate (SSA 1842(c)(2); 42 CFR 405.922). The rate is 4.75% for Jul-Dec 2026 and was 4.125% for Jan-Jun 2026.
- Redetermination: 60 days, plus up to 14 days for each later evidence submission (405.950; 405.946(b)).
- QIC: 60 days. ALJ: 90 days (180 if escalated). Medicare Appeals Council: 90 days (180 if escalated).
- Favorable decisions: the MAC must pay within 30 days (MCPM Ch. 29 sections 310.11, 320.9, 330.4).
- Written provider inquiries: answered within 45 business days. Congressional inquiries: within 10 business days (Pub. 100-09 Ch. 6 section 70.2.2).
- Reopenings it accepts: the MAC aims to finish in 60 days (MCPM Ch. 34 section 10.7). Reopening itself is discretionary, and a refusal cannot be appealed.

WHAT HAPPENS IF THEY DO NOT? It depends on the level.
- Redetermination: if the MAC misses 60 days there is no interest, no deemed decision and no escalation. The statute and regulation have no consequence clause, and a QIC dismisses a reconsideration filed before a redetermination exists (405.972(b)(6)).
- From the QIC up, a missed deadline lets the appellant escalate: QIC to ALJ (405.970), ALJ to Council (405.1016(e)-(f)), Council to federal court (405.1132).
- Interest: none on full denials, and none on denied claims later paid on appeal (MCPM Ch. 1 section 80.2.2.1(C)). There is no form for claiming interest, because the MAC computes it and reports it on the RA.

WHAT REAL LEVERAGE EXISTS. A MAC is a federal contractor. Veiled threats have no legal teeth against it. These do:
1. File a request that cannot be dismissed: include the four elements of 405.944(b) and note that the MAC may not dismiss a request that substantially complies (MCPM Ch. 29 section 310.1.B).
2. Route each item to the right track. Clerical and minor errors go to reopening: math errors, 'misapplication of a fee schedule', duplicates, modifier/POS/units/date data errors (405.980(a)(3); MCPM Ch. 34 section 10.4). Coverage, medical necessity and payment disputes go to redetermination.
3. Name the decision date (60 days) and the 30-day payment date in the letter.
4. Ask for the specific policy, manual or regulation provision the MAC relied on (SSA 1869(a)(4)(C), (a)(5)(C)).
5. Put all evidence in by the QIC. Provider evidence first offered at the ALJ is excluded unless there is good cause (405.966(a)(2), 405.1018(c), 405.1028).
6. Use the escalation rights at the QIC, ALJ and Council levels.
7. On takebacks, a timely redetermination stops recoupment (405.379). If the overpayment is reversed at the ALJ or above, recouped money earns interest (405.378(j)).
8. Pressure outside the appeal: the 45- and 10-business-day inquiry clocks; provider satisfaction is a MAC contract standard (SSA 1874A(b)(3)); CMS takes feedback about CGS at OPOLE_IFM_CHIKCGP@cms.hhs.gov. Keep PHI out of email.

A caution for the letter tone: the MAC reviewer is bound by CMS policy and may not change the Physician Fee Schedule amount (MCPM Ch. 29 section 310). Arguments should show that CMS policy requires payment. The QIC and ALJ are not bound by LCDs or manuals, so policy-validity arguments belong there.

WHERE TO SEND THINGS.
- CGS J15 Part B does not accept faxed redeterminations (CGS job aid revised 12/16/2025). Use myCGS (one claim per request; up to 10 PDFs, 40 MB each, 150 MB total) or mail to PO Box 20018, Nashville. Written CGS reopenings are mail-only, one claim per form.
- WPS J8 accepts faxed redeterminations with the Indiana cover sheet. Its two current forms list different Indiana fax numbers: 608-224-3502 on the redetermination form and 608-224-3504 on the overpayment form. Confirm before automating.
- The WPS portal takes Part B redeterminations and one-time clerical error reopenings.
- Both Part B MACs send reconsiderations to C2C QIC Part B North: fax 904-539-4081, portal, or PO Box 45208.
- ALJ requests go through the OMHA e-Appeal portal. The ALJ amount in controversy is $200 for 2026 and 2027.

COST CONTROL. Medicare may not charge a fee for physician-service appeals (SSA 1842(c)(4)), so labor is the only cost. For cents-level items, the near-zero-labor route is a portal clerical reopening for MAC pricing or data errors within 1 year. Redeterminations are one claim at a time in both portals. CMS allows one paper request covering several beneficiaries (MCPM Ch. 29 section 300.5.B), but the MAC may split it, and at CGS paper means mail. Requesting a reopening does not stop the 120-day appeal clock, and resubmitting a claim does not restart it. Do not chase the 2% sequestration cut (CARC 253); it is statutory (2 USC 901a).

rules.quote: any request for redetermination must be filed within 120 calendar days from the date a party receives the notice of the initial determination ... presumed to be 5 calendar days after the date of the notice ... The request is considered as filed on the date it is received by the contractor.
rules.applies_to: Traditional Medicare Part A/B claims processed by a MAC (CGS J15, WPS J8; Palmetto for Railroad beneficiaries). Parties: assigned/participating physician-supplier and beneficiary (405.906). Not Medicare Advantage, not Medicaid.
rules.requires: The MAC must accept and process a timely, valid request; the provider must get it to the MAC (not just mail it) by day 120 after receipt of the RA. Late requests need a written good-cause explanation (405.942(b)(1)).
rules.deadline: 120 calendar days from receipt of the RA/MSN; receipt presumed RA date + 5 days; filed = date received in the MAC mailroom, by fax, or in the portal (MCPM 29 sec. 310.2); weekend/holiday deadlines roll to the next work day (MCPM 29 sec. 310.2).
rules.consequence: Late request is dismissed (405.952(b)(3)) unless good cause. For providers good cause is narrow: incorrect information from CMS/MAC/SSA or unavoidable events such as disasters; failure of a billing company or other consultant is NOT good cause (MCPM 29 sec. 240.3).
rules.provider_use: Compute every Medicare due date as RA date + 125 days rolled to the next business day, and file through the portal so receipt is same-day. Never let a reopening attempt run past this date (a reopening request does not toll the appeal clock, MCPM 34 sec. 10).

rules.quote: The request for redetermination must be in writing and should be made on a standard CMS form. A written request that is not made on a standard CMS form is accepted if it contains the same required elements ... (1) The beneficiary's name; (2) The Medicare number; (3) Specific service(s) and/or item(s) ... and the specific date(s) of the service; (4) The name of the party or the representative of the party.
rules.applies_to: All Part A/B redetermination requests to CGS and WPS.
rules.requires: MAC must accept either CMS-20027, its own MAC form, or a letter with the four elements; MCPM 29 sec. 310.1.B: where the elements appear in attachments 'the request substantially complies ... MACs shall not dismiss requests under 42 CFR 405.952(b)(2)'. Must be filed with the contractor named on the RA (405.944(a)). A provider letter counts as a request if it has the elements and asks for action or states dissatisfaction.
rules.deadline: Within the 120-day window (MFFS-01).
rules.consequence: A provider request missing elements is treated as incomplete and dismissed with an explanation (MCPM 29 sec. 310.1.B.3); dismissal can be vacated or reviewed (MFFS-06).
rules.provider_use: Generate every request from one template that always prints the four elements plus ICN, line, CPT/HCPCS, billed and paid amounts; attach the RA page with the line highlighted. Signature is no longer required (CGS level-1 page: 'As of July 8, 2019, CMS no longer requires a signature on an appeal form'). CGS asks that written requests be 'typed and submitted on the Medicare Part B Jurisdiction 15 Redetermination Request Form' and to 'Always submit the Appeal form as the top document'; the WPS J8 form marks 'All fields are REQUIRED' and says incomplete requests will be dismissed.

rules.quote: a party must explain why it disagrees with the contractor's determination and should include any evidence ... When a party submits additional evidence after filing the request for redetermination, the contractor's 60 calendar day decision-making time frame is automatically extended for up to 14 calendar days for each submission.
rules.applies_to: All redeterminations.
rules.requires: Explanation of disagreement and evidence with the request.
rules.deadline: Each later submission adds up to 14 calendar days to the MAC's 60-day clock.
rules.consequence: Piecemeal evidence slows the decision; a portal at WPS will not accept documents after submission ('you cannot submit it after you submit the request').
rules.provider_use: Send one complete packet (note, op report/Mohs map, path report, RA) with the request; never send follow-up pages unless asked.

rules.quote: The contractor mails, or otherwise transmits, written notice of the redetermination or dismissal to the parties ... within 60 calendar days of the date the contractor receives a timely filed request for redetermination. [Statute:] Redeterminations shall be concluded by not later than the 60-day period beginning on the date the fiscal intermediary or the carrier ... receives a request for a redetermination.
rules.applies_to: CGS J15 and WPS J8 redeterminations (Part B).
rules.requires: MAC must decide and mail/transmit notice within 60 days of receipt (plus 14-day extensions per later evidence submission; later of receipt or extension grant for late-filed requests).
rules.deadline: 60 calendar days from MAC receipt of a timely request.
rules.consequence: None stated. Unlike 1869(c)(3)(C)(ii) (QIC) and 1869(d)(3) (ALJ/DAB), the statute attaches no consequence to a missed redetermination deadline, and Subpart I gives no escalation from the MAC level; a QIC dismisses a reconsideration request 'When the contractor has not issued a redetermination' (405.972(b)(6)). No interest, no deemed approval. (Conclusion from reading statute, regulation and MCPM 29 in full; MCPM 29 mentions escalation only at QIC level and above.)
rules.provider_use: In the letter, state the receipt-based decision date. If day 60 (+ extensions) passes: send a written status inquiry (45-business-day answer duty, MFFS-24); for chronic lateness use CMS feedback / Congressional office (MFFS-24, MFFS-25). Do not file at the QIC early.

rules.quote: (1) A clear statement indicating the extent to which the redetermination is favorable or unfavorable; (2) A summary of the facts ...; (3) An explanation of how pertinent laws, regulations, coverage rules, and CMS policies apply to the facts of the case; ... (6) A statement of any specific missing documentation that must be submitted with a request for a reconsideration ... [Statute 1869(a)(5)(C):] may obtain, upon request, information on the specific provision of the policy, manual, or regulation used in making the redetermination.
rules.applies_to: MAC redetermination notices (affirmations in whole or part); RA as notice of initial determination (405.921(b)).
rules.requires: Unfavorable/partly unfavorable MRN must contain all listed elements, including notice of reconsideration rights and the full-and-early-evidence warning; RA must give basis of denial and CARC/RARC codes (405.921(b)(2)). On request, the MAC must identify the specific policy/manual/regulation provision used.
rules.deadline: Within the 60-day redetermination clock (405.956(a)(1)).
rules.consequence: No penalty stated for a defective notice; a missing element is an argument at the QIC (de novo, 405.968(a)) and a basis to request the specific provision.
rules.provider_use: Parse each MRN for item (6) 'missing documentation' and auto-add it to the QIC packet; when a denial is vague, request the specific provision under 1869(a)(5)(C) / (a)(4)(C) in writing.

rules.quote: If good and sufficient cause is established, a contractor may vacate its dismissal of a request for redetermination within 180 calendar days from the date of the notice of dismissal. ... [405.974(b)(1)] files a written request for review of the dismissal with the QIC within 60 calendar days after receipt of the contractor's notice of dismissal.
rules.applies_to: Dismissed redetermination requests (incomplete, untimely, wrong party, no initial determination).
rules.requires: MAC dismissal notice must state the right to ask the MAC to vacate (405.952(c)).
rules.deadline: Vacate request: within 180 days of the dismissal notice; QIC review of dismissal: within 60 days of receipt (presumed notice date + 5).
rules.consequence: QIC review of a MAC dismissal is binding and not further reviewable (405.974(b)(3)); if the QIC finds the dismissal wrong it remands for a redetermination.
rules.provider_use: Treat every dismissal as a fix-and-resend task: cure the missing element and ask the MAC to vacate (cheaper), keep the QIC-review date as a backstop.

rules.quote: If the redetermination decision is fully or partially favorable to the appellant and gives a specific amount to be paid, the MAC effectuates within 30 calendar days of the date of the redetermination decision. If ... the payment amount must be computed or recomputed, the MAC effectuates the decision within 30 days after the payment amount is determined ... no later than 30 calendar days after the date of the redetermination decision.
rules.applies_to: Favorable MAC redeterminations; QIC and OMHA decisions (30 days from receipt of the effectuation notice); Appeals Council (initiate within 30, complete within 60 days).
rules.requires: MAC must adjust the claim, pay, and issue a revised RA.
rules.deadline: 30 calendar days (computation by day 30, payment within 30 days after computation).
rules.consequence: Manual instruction; no interest or penalty specified in the manual for late effectuation (405.378 underpayment interest may apply only if a 'written determination of an underpayment' is unpaid after 30 days - unconfirmed, see open questions).
rules.provider_use: Track favorable decisions to payment; on day 31 send a written inquiry citing MCPM 29 sec. 310.11.

rules.quote: any request for a reconsideration must be filed within 180 calendar days from the date the party receives the notice of the redetermination ... considered as filed on the date it is received by the QIC. ... (5) The name of the contractor that made the redetermination.
rules.applies_to: Any party dissatisfied with a MAC redetermination; for CGS J15 and WPS J8 Part B the QIC is C2C Innovative Solutions, QIC Part B North (CGS reconsideration form; WPS appeal-rights sheet 06/06/2023).
rules.requires: Written request on CMS-20033 or a letter with the five elements; file with the QIC named on the MRN; no amount-in-controversy minimum.
rules.deadline: 180 calendar days from receipt of the redetermination (presumed notice date + 5); 60 days if reviewing a MAC dismissal.
rules.consequence: Late -> QIC dismissal (405.972(b)(3)) unless good cause.
rules.provider_use: QIC accepts fax (904-539-4081) and portal - fits a fax-based pipeline; send the complete evidence set (MFFS-09).

rules.quote: Absent good cause, failure to submit all evidence, including documentation requested in the notice of redetermination prior to the issuance of the notice of reconsideration precludes subsequent consideration of that evidence.
rules.applies_to: Providers/suppliers and beneficiaries represented by providers (not unrepresented beneficiaries).
rules.requires: All evidence must be in the record before the QIC decides; new provider evidence at OMHA needs a written explanation and a good-cause finding or it is excluded.
rules.deadline: Before the QIC issues its reconsideration.
rules.consequence: Evidence excluded at the ALJ and Council levels ('must exclude the evidence', 405.1028(a)(3)).
rules.provider_use: The QIC packet is the last real chance to add evidence; automate a checklist from the MRN's missing-documentation statement.

rules.quote: Notify the parties that it cannot complete the reconsideration by the deadline ... and offer the appellant the opportunity to escalate the appeal to OMHA. [Statute:] In the case of a failure by the qualified independent contractor to mail the notice of the decision by the end of the period ... the party ... may request a hearing before the Secretary, notwithstanding any requirements for a reconsidered determination.
rules.applies_to: QIC Part B North (C2C) reconsiderations of CGS/WPS redeterminations.
rules.requires: QIC decides within 60 days (+14 days per late evidence submission); if it cannot, it must notify and offer escalation; on a written escalation request it must decide or forward the file to OMHA within 5 calendar days.
rules.deadline: 60 calendar days from QIC receipt; 5 calendar days after a written escalation request (or after the period ends).
rules.consequence: Appellant may escalate to an ALJ without a QIC decision (amount in controversy still required); OMHA then has 180 days (405.1016(c)).
rules.provider_use: Calendar day 61; for high-dollar items send the escalation request in writing to the QIC as soon as the window closes.

rules.quote: The calendar year 2026 AIC threshold amounts are $200 for ALJ hearings and $1,960 for judicial review. ... The calendar year 2027 AIC threshold amounts are $200 for ALJ hearings and $2,000 for judicial review. [405.1016(a)] no later than the end of the 90 calendar day period beginning on the date the request for hearing is received
rules.applies_to: Parties to a QIC reconsideration (or escalated QIC case) with enough amount remaining in controversy.
rules.requires: Written request (OMHA-100 or letter with 405.1014(a) elements) within 60 days of receipt of the QIC decision, with copies to all other parties who got the QIC notice and proof of that (405.1014(d)); amount in controversy = charges minus Medicare payment and collectible deductible/coinsurance (405.1006(d)). One appellant may aggregate claims for 'similar or related services' in one request filed within 60 days of the last reconsideration (405.1006(e)(1)).
rules.deadline: File within 60 days of receipt; ALJ decides within 90 days of receipt (180 if escalated from the QIC).
rules.consequence: If OMHA misses its period, the appellant may escalate to the Council by written request; OMHA then decides within 5 days or forwards the file (405.1016(e)-(f)). ALJ reviews de novo and is not bound by LCDs or manual instructions (405.1000(d), 405.1062(a)).
rules.provider_use: Use aggregation to lift many small, same-issue denials over $200; file through the OMHA e-Appeal Portal (https://hhs-ecape-portal.entellitrak.com). Copying each beneficiary is a real per-case cost to budget.

rules.quote: The Council issues a final decision or dismissal order or remands a case ... within 90 calendar days of receipt of the appellant's request for review ... [405.1132(b)] A party may file an action in a Federal district court within 60 calendar days after the date it receives the Council's notice that the Council is not able to issue a final decision
rules.applies_to: Parties to an ALJ/attorney adjudicator decision or escalated case; court review needs AIC $1,960 (requests in 2026) / $2,000 (2027).
rules.requires: Request Council review within 60 days of receipt of the ALJ decision; Council decides within 90 days (180 if escalated from OMHA).
rules.deadline: 60 days to request; 90/180 days for the Council; 60 days to sue after a Council decision or a no-decision notice.
rules.consequence: Escalation to federal district court if the Council misses its period (405.1132).
rules.provider_use: Rarely economic for derm claim-level disputes; relevant only for large aggregated or extrapolated overpayment cases.

rules.quote: a contractor must process clerical errors (which includes minor errors and omissions) as reopenings, instead of as redeterminations ... (i) Mathematical or computational mistakes; (ii) Inaccurate data entry; or (iii) Denials of claims as duplicates. ... A party may request that a contractor reopen its initial determination ... within 1 year from the date of the initial determination ... for any reason. [MCPM 34 sec. 10.4 list adds:] Misapplication of a fee schedule; ... Incorrect data items, such as provider number, use of a modifier or date of service.
rules.applies_to: Any party to a MAC initial determination or redetermination (CGS, WPS).
rules.requires: Clerical/minor errors must go through reopening, not appeal. Reopening is discretionary for the MAC; once a party-requested reopening is accepted, MCPM 34 sec. 10.7 sets a 60-day completion target (except 'big box' requests of 40+ beneficiaries/claims and $40,000+).
rules.deadline: 1 year from the date of the initial determination for any reason; 4 years for good cause (MFFS-14); any time for a clerical error on an unfavorable determination (405.980(c)(3)), though CMS says such late requests should be granted 'rarely' (MCPM 34 sec. 10.6.2). The WPS portal manual words the 1-year limit as from 'receipt of the initial Remittance Notice'.
rules.consequence: Decision whether to reopen 'is binding and not subject to appeal' (405.980(a)(5)); reopening does not toll the 120-day appeal clock (MCPM 34 sec. 10); a revised determination gets new appeal rights only for the revised portion (405.984(f)). If the MAC disagrees it is clerical, it must dismiss the reopening and advise of appeal rights if still timely (405.980(a)(3)). Omissions do not include unbilled services (MCPM 34 sec. 10.4).
rules.provider_use: Cheapest Medicare recovery path: misapplied fee schedule, wrong units, modifier 25/59/79, POS, dx pointer, duplicate denials. Use the portal (myCGS automated reopenings; WPS CER) within 1 year; file a redetermination instead when the issue needs medical review or when the 120-day window is about to close.

rules.quote: Good cause may be established when- (1) There is new and material evidence that- (i) Was not available or known at the time of the determination or decision; and (ii) May result in a different conclusion; or (2) The evidence that was considered in making the determination or decision clearly shows on its face that an obvious error was made
rules.applies_to: Party-requested reopenings 1-4 years after the initial determination or redetermination.
rules.requires: Party must show new and material evidence or an error obvious on the face of the record; third-party payer error is expressly not good cause (405.986(c)); a change in CMS policy is not a basis (405.986(b)).
rules.deadline: Within 4 years from the date of the initial determination or redetermination.
rules.consequence: Refusal not appealable.
rules.provider_use: Use for old MAC pricing errors that are provable from the RA and the published fee schedule ('error on the face of the evidence', MCPM 34 sec. 10.11.3).

rules.quote: When a party has filed a valid request for an appeal ... no adjudicator has jurisdiction to reopen an issue on a claim that is under appeal until all appeal rights for that issue are exhausted.
rules.applies_to: Any claim with a pending appeal.
rules.requires: Pick one track per issue.
rules.deadline: n/a
rules.consequence: Parallel reopening requests are ineffective.
rules.provider_use: The worklist must lock a claim/issue once an appeal is filed so the system never sends a duplicate reopening.

rules.quote: If a contractor issues a denial of a claim because it did not receive requested documentation during medical review and the party subsequently requests a redetermination, the contractor must process the request as a reopening.
rules.applies_to: Claims denied CO-50 with RARC M127 after an unanswered Additional Documentation Request (MAC 45 days; UPIC 30 days).
rules.requires: File the redetermination with the records within 120 days; the appeals unit routes it to medical review as a reopening (MCPM 34 sec. 10.3).
rules.deadline: ADR response 45 calendar days (MAC) / 30 (UPIC); request within 120 days of the denial.
rules.consequence: If affirmed, the provider keeps redetermination rights, with 120 days measured from the medical-review decision (MCPM 34 sec. 10.3).
rules.provider_use: Detect CO-50/M127 on the 835 and auto-build a records packet.

rules.quote: If payment is not issued, mailed, or otherwise transmitted within the applicable number of calendar days ... after a clean claim ... is received, interest shall be paid at the rate used for purposes of section 3902(a) of title 31 ... for the period beginning on the day after the required payment date and ending on the date on which payment is made. [Treasury:] The Prompt Payment interest rate for July 1- December 31, 2026 is 4.75%.
rules.applies_to: Clean, non-PIP Part A/B claims paid by a MAC (30 calendar days for claims received after 10/1/1993). Applies to traditional Medicare only.
rules.requires: MAC must pay interest automatically, computed as payment x rate x days / 365 (366 in leap year) on the net payment after deductible, coinsurance and MSP; rate applicable on the day of payment; reported per claim on the remittance (MCPM Ch. 1 sec. 80.2.2).
rules.deadline: Payment due by day 30 after receipt (count starts the day after receipt); interest runs from day 31 to the payment date. Rates: Jan-Jun 2026 4.125% (91 FR 5035); Jul-Dec 2026 4.75% (91 FR 42594).
rules.consequence: Interest owed by statute; no penalty beyond interest; no provider claim form or procedure found.
rules.provider_use: Do not chase interest by letter routinely: verify the MAC paid it by comparing receipt date (277CA) with the 835 payment date and the interest reported. MCPM's own example: $100 paid 3 days late at 5.625% = $0.05; at 4.75% it is about $0.04, so this lever only matters in aggregate or for MAC-wide delays.

rules.citation: MCPM Pub. 100-04 Ch. 1 sec. 80.2.2 and sec. 80.2.2.1(C)-(D); sec. 80.2 (clean claim definition); 42 USC 1395u(c)(2)(B)(i)
rules.quote: Interest is not paid on: Claims requiring external investigation or development ...; Claims on which no payment is due; Full denials; Claims for which the provider is receiving PIP ... Interest payments are not payable on clean claims initially processed to denial and on which payment is made subsequent to the initial decision as a result of an appeal request.
rules.applies_to: Traditional Medicare claims.
rules.requires: No interest on denied-then-overturned claims; partial postpayment denials reduce interest proportionally (80.2.2.1(D)).
rules.deadline: n/a
rules.consequence: Appeal wins do not carry clean-claim interest.
rules.provider_use: Do not promise interest in Medicare appeal letters; it is a lever only for slow initial payment of clean claims.

rules.quote: no payment shall be issued, mailed, or otherwise transmitted with respect to any claim ... within the applicable number of calendar days after the date on which the claim is received ... (i) with respect to claims submitted electronically ... 13 days, and (ii) with respect to claims submitted otherwise, 28 days.
rules.applies_to: All MAC claims (no-payment claims and PIP excepted per manual).
rules.requires: MAC may not pay before the floor.
rules.deadline: Electronic: no payment within 13 days of receipt (manual: payable from the 14th day); paper: 28 days by statute (manual table: 29th day).
rules.consequence: Explains normal Medicare payment timing; a claim unpaid at day 14-29 is not late.
rules.provider_use: Set the 'unanswered Medicare claim' alarm after day 30 from receipt (interest window), not earlier.

rules.quote: CMS will charge interest on overpayments, and pay interest on underpayments, to providers and suppliers of services (including physicians and other practitioners) ... If an intermediary or a carrier makes a final determination that an underpayment exists, interest to the provider or the supplier will accrue from the date of notification of the underpayment. ... Interest charges will be waived if the overpayment or underpayment is completely liquidated within 30 days from the date of the final determination.
rules.applies_to: Part B physicians/suppliers where a MAC issues a written determination of an underpayment.
rules.requires: Interest on an unpaid determined underpayment for each full 30-day period after notification, at the higher of the Treasury private consumer rate or the current value of funds rate.
rules.deadline: Waived if paid within 30 days of the final determination.
rules.consequence: Interest for each full 30-day period of delay after a written underpayment determination.
rules.provider_use: Secondary lever when a MAC admits an underpayment in writing but does not pay within 30 days. Whether a favorable redetermination letter counts as 'a written determination of an underpayment' is not stated (open question).

rules.quote: Medicare contractors can begin recoupment no earlier than 41 days from the date of the initial overpayment demand but shall cease recoupment of the overpayment in question, upon receipt of a timely and valid request for a redetermination of an overpayment. If the recoupment has not yet gone into effect, the contractor shall not initiate recoupment.
rules.applies_to: Post-payment Part B overpayment demands (and listed MSP recoveries) appealable as revised initial determinations.
rules.requires: Recoupment stops on a timely valid redetermination request and again on a timely valid reconsideration request; it may resume on day 60 after an affirming redetermination unless a reconsideration is filed; at ALJ and above recoupment continues, but if reversed the MAC pays simple interest on recouped principal for full 30-day periods (405.378(j)).
rules.deadline: File the redetermination before day 41 after the demand to prevent recoupment from starting; reconsideration within 60 days of the redetermination to keep it stopped (405.379(e)(1)(ii), (e)(2)).
rules.consequence: Money recouped before a valid request may be retained pending the outcome (405.379(g)).
rules.provider_use: Real leverage on takebacks. Flag Medicare overpayment demands on intake; WPS portal has a 'appealing an overpayment' flag that pauses collection; CGS overpayment form/fax for offsets 615.664.5916 (KY).

rules.quote: section 1848(i)(1) of the Act prohibits administrative and judicial review of the individual components used to compute Medicare physician fee schedule payment amounts. However, a payment amount determination with respect to a particular item or service on a claim is an initial determination that is appealable.
rules.applies_to: Traditional Medicare.
rules.requires: Underpayment of a specific line is appealable (405.924(b)(11): 'whether there was an underpayment of benefits ... and if so, the amount'); the fee schedule itself, refusals to reopen, timely-filing determinations and rejected/incomplete claims are not.
rules.deadline: n/a
rules.consequence: Appeals of non-appealable matters are dismissed. The MAC reviewer 'may not change the amount required to be paid under the Physician Fee Schedule' (MCPM 29 sec. 310). Duplicate denials have no appeal rights unless the supplier disputes that it was a duplicate (MCPM 29 sec. 200 NOTE).
rules.provider_use: Classify before acting: wrong application of the MPFS (locality, POS facility/non-facility, MPPR, units) is chaseable; disagreement with the MPFS rate is not.

rules.quote: the claim must be filed no later than the close of the period ending 1 calendar year after the date of service. [MCPM Ch. 1 sec. 70.6:] Where the provider or supplier is protesting the denial of payment or the assignment of responsibility, no formal channels of appeal are available. However, the contractor may, at the request of the provider or supplier, informally review its initial determination.
rules.applies_to: Never-billed or rejected Medicare claims (unanswered claims, unbilled lines).
rules.requires: File within 1 calendar year of the date of service (line 'From' date for professional claims); exceptions only for MAC/CMS error or misrepresentation, retroactive entitlement, Medicaid or MA retroactive recoupment (extensions to end of 6th month after notice; error exception barred if requested more than 4 years after DOS).
rules.deadline: 1 calendar year after DOS; rolls to next workday if on a Federal nonworkday (424.44(c)).
rules.consequence: Late claims denied; the timely-filing denial is not appealable (405.926(n)).
rules.provider_use: Unanswered Medicare claims must be refiled (not appealed) before the 1-year mark; a rejected/unprocessable claim was never 'received' (MCPM Ch. 1 sec. 80.2.1).

rules.citation: Medicare Contractor Beneficiary and Provider Communications Manual, Pub. 100-09 Ch. 6 secs. 30.7.4.1, 70.2.2.1, 70.2.2.4 (Rev. 13683, 04-08-26); MCPM Ch. 29 sec. 310.1.A.1
rules.quote: All general written provider inquiries (including those received electronically) shall be responded to in writing or by telephone within 45 business days of receipt. ... All Congressional written inquiries shall be responded to in writing within 10 business days of receipt.
rules.applies_to: MACs (CGS, WPS) answering provider correspondence and Congressional offices.
rules.requires: Final or interim response within 45 business days for provider inquiries; 10 business days for Congressional inquiries; final response within 5 business days after needed information arrives.
rules.deadline: 45 business days (provider); 10 business days (Congressional).
rules.consequence: Manual/contract standard; no payment penalty.
rules.provider_use: Use a written inquiry for status, missing interest, unexplained payment amounts. For a systemic or stuck problem, a U.S. Representative's or Senator's caseworker inquiry gets a 10-business-day answer clock; CGS has dedicated Congressional fax lines (KY 615.664.5913, Congressional offices only). Inquiries are not appeals and do not stop the 120-day clock.

rules.quote: The Secretary shall include, as one of the standards developed under subparagraph (A), provider and beneficiary satisfaction levels. ... All contractor performance requirements shall be set forth in the contract ... (ii) shall be used for evaluating contractor performance under the contract
rules.applies_to: All MACs, including CGS (J15) and WPS (J8).
rules.requires: CMS must set and measure MAC performance requirements, including provider satisfaction, and publish performance to the extent possible.
rules.deadline: n/a
rules.consequence: Contract evaluation; no claim-level remedy for the provider.
rules.provider_use: Legitimate non-threat pressure: a documented, factual note that a pattern of missed redetermination deadlines or incorrect pricing will be reported to CMS (CGS lists OPOLE_IFM_CHIKCGP@cms.hhs.gov for feedback about CGS). Keep it factual and PHI-free.

rules.quote: Neither a medicare administrative contractor nor the Secretary may impose a fee under this subchapter- (A) for the filing of claims related to physicians' services, (B) for an error in filing a claim ... (C) for any appeal under this subchapter with respect to physicians' services ... (E) for responding to inquiries respecting physicians' services
rules.applies_to: Physicians' services under Part B.
rules.requires: No MAC charges for appeals, inquiries or claim errors.
rules.deadline: n/a
rules.consequence: Marginal cost of a Medicare appeal/reopening is the practice's own labor and postage only.
rules.provider_use: ROI model for Medicare items = recovery probability x amount - (labor minutes x rate + postage if CGS paper). Portal clerical reopenings approach zero labor when automated.

rules.quote: A supplier who has accepted assignment for items or services furnished to a beneficiary that are at issue in the claim.
rules.applies_to: Physician practices billing on assignment (participating); non-participating physicians not billing on assignment only for 1842(l) refund situations.
rules.requires: The practice is a party in its own right on assigned claims; the beneficiary is also a party and receives copies of unfavorable decisions.
rules.deadline: n/a
rules.consequence: Unassigned claims: no provider appeal except as the beneficiary's representative (CMS-1696) or under 405.906(b)(4).
rules.provider_use: File in the practice's own name (the practice is the party on assigned claims; no appointment of representative needed). MCPM Ch. 29 sec. 310.1.B.5: a request 'submitted by an individual (who is not an appointed or authorized representative), filed on behalf of a provider ... and the request does not include an appointment instrument' is treated as an inquiry, not an appeal - so an outside billing company must file with a valid appointment (405.910) or the request will not count.

rules.quote: The contractor may raise and develop new issues that are relevant to the claims in the particular case. [MCPM:] if the appellant questions the amount paid, the contractor must also review medical necessity, coverage, deductible, and limitation on liability, if applicable.
rules.applies_to: Redeterminations, especially of payment-amount disputes and automated prepayment denials.
rules.requires: For claims denied after complex pre/post-payment or automated post-payment review the MAC limits review to the original denial reasons; for automated prepayment denials it may develop new issues and deny for other reasons.
rules.deadline: n/a
rules.consequence: An appeal of a few cents can expose the whole line to medical-necessity review and a worse result.
rules.provider_use: Before filing a payment-amount redetermination, confirm the note supports the service; prefer a clerical reopening for pure pricing/data errors.

rules.quote: the date of the first MSN or RA that states the coverage and payment decision is the date of the initial determination. Adjustments to the initial claim or claim resubmissions for the same item/service on the same date of service that are included on subsequent MSNs or RAs, but do not revise the initial determination, do not extend/change the appeal rights on the initial determination.
rules.applies_to: Medicare claims that were resubmitted or adjusted.
rules.requires: Appeal clock runs from the first RA with the decision.
rules.deadline: 120 days from the first decision RA.
rules.consequence: Late appeals dismissed even if a later RA repeats the denial.
rules.provider_use: Key the deadline to the earliest 835 for that line, not the latest.

rules.quote: initial determinations shall be concluded by not later than the 45-day period beginning on the date the fiscal intermediary or the carrier, as the case may be, receives a claim for benefits ... Subparagraph (A) shall not apply with respect to any claim that is subject to the requirements of section 1395h(c)(2) or 1395u(c)(2)
rules.applies_to: Non-clean claims (those needing development).
rules.requires: Initial determination within 45 days of receipt.
rules.deadline: 45 days from receipt.
rules.consequence: No consequence or interest stated in the statute for missing it.
rules.provider_use: For a Medicare claim pending in development past 45 days, a written inquiry is the only lever.

batch_and_channel: Form vs letter: 42 CFR 405.944(b) - the request 'should be made on a standard CMS form' (CMS-20027) but a letter with the four elements must be accepted; MCPM Ch. 29 sec. 310.1.B.2 also accepts a MAC-approved portal submission. CGS and WPS publish their own forms (CGS J15 Redetermination Request Form; WPS J8 Part B Redetermination Request Form 02/19/26, 'All fields are REQUIRED'). Signature not required since July 8, 2019 (CGS level-1 page; C2C QIC page).

Several claims or beneficiaries in one request: allowed by CMS - MCPM Ch. 29 sec. 300.5.B: 'If a party files a request for redetermination that involves claims of multiple beneficiaries ... the MAC may process the appeal by issuing a separate decision letter for each beneficiary's claim(s) (i.e., as a split appeal), or ... a single letter with attachments'. Each beneficiary still gets the decision for his/her claims. Overpayments with a single account receivable get one letter (300.5.A). The MAC may split, so the time saved is on the practice side only.

MAC forms and portals are per claim: myCGS redetermination is launched from one claim's detail page; CGS written reopening forms: 'Only one claim can be corrected per form; up to 12 line items per claim' and 'Submit only one claim per request form'; WPS portal redetermination and CER are per claim. 'Big box' reopening requests (40+ beneficiaries/claims and $40,000+) are exempt from the 60-day completion target (MCPM 34 sec. 10.7).

CGS J15 Part B (Kentucky) redeterminations: NO FAX - CGS job aid (rev. 12/16/2025): 'Redeterminations do not accept faxed request.' Preferred: myCGS portal ('the preferred method'). Mail: CGS, Attn: J15 Part B Appeals Department, PO Box 20018, Nashville, TN 37202 (form footer; addresses page lists J15 - Part A/B Correspondence, PO Box 20018). FedEx/UPS/certified: 26 Century Blvd Suite NT600, Nashville, TN 37214.

myCGS redetermination limits: must be within 120 days and claim finalized; reason field up to 1,200 characters; at least one attachment; up to 10 PDF documents, each up to 40 MB, total 150 MB; e-signature; confirmation plus Submission ID; decision letters viewable in the portal (myCGS user manual, appeals section). The myCGS manual describes portal reconsideration requests only for 'Part A and HHH users'; for Part B send reconsiderations to the QIC.

CGS reopenings: myCGS Reopenings is 'the BEST vehicle' and can adjust claims 'without manual intervention'; hardcopy forms (e.g., BPC 346 billed amount/procedure code, GRF 679 general) mailed to J15 - Part B Correspondence, CGS, Attn: Reopenings, PO Box 20018, Nashville, TN 37202; 'Written Reopenings may take up to 60 days'; questions about amount paid, status requests and 'reprocess' requests without a specific error are treated as inquiries and returned.

CGS fax numbers that do exist (phone/fax page updated 10.27.2026): General Correspondence 615.782.4490; Overpayment Recovery offset requests and OPR forms - Kentucky 615.664.5916; Congressional offices only - KY 615.664.5913. General written inquiries by mail to PO Box 20018; 'CMS guidelines allow up to 45 business days to respond.'

WPS J8 Part B (Indiana) redeterminations: portal (WPS SNAP manual, Nov 2026: per claim, select lines, overpayment flag pauses recoupment, documents only at submission, 100 MB max, up to 20 files in one .zip, tracking number); fax with the 'Indiana Appeals/Clerical Error Reopening Fax Cover Sheet' - Indiana fax listed as (608) 224-3502 on the redetermination form dated 02/19/26 but (608) 224-3504 on the overpayment redetermination form dated 02/18/2026 (conflict, confirm before automating); mail: WPS Government Services, ATTN: Redeterminations (or ATTN: Overpayment Appeals), PO Box 8580, Madison, WI 53708-8580.

WPS clerical error reopenings (CER) in the portal: Part B MCS claims; allowed - units increase without billed increase, add/change/delete modifiers incl. 24, 25, 57, 58, 59, 76, 78, 79, 95, place of service, diagnosis, billed amount, rendering NPI, procedure codes, DOS within same year; excluded - adding lines, raising both units and billed amount, rejected/unprocessable claims, ADR no-response denials, claims with modifiers 22/23/53/55/62/66/74/CR or NOC/drug codes, previously adjusted claims; 'providers can only reopen a claim once via the portal'; after 1 year request in writing with good cause.

QIC (2nd level) for both CGS J15 and WPS J8 Part B: C2C Innovative Solutions, QIC Part B North - fax 904-539-4081, portal https://www.c2cinc.com/QIC-Part-B-North, mail PO Box 45208, Jacksonville, FL 32232-5208 (CMS second-level page modified 09/30/2026; C2C page; WPS appeal-rights sheet 06/06/2023: 'Part B J5 and J8: C2C ... QIC Part B North'; CGS reconsideration form). Use CMS-20033 or a letter with the five 405.964(b) elements; always follow the QIC named on the MRN.

ALJ (3rd level): OMHA-100 or a written request with 405.1014(a) elements, filed with the office named on the QIC decision or via the OMHA e-Appeal Portal https://hhs-ecape-portal.entellitrak.com; must send copies to all parties who got the QIC decision and prove it (405.1014(d)); one appellant can aggregate claims for similar or related services in one request filed within 60 days of the last reconsideration (405.1006(e)); consolidated hearings at ALJ discretion (405.1044).

Filing date = receipt: redetermination filed when received by the MAC (405.942(a)(2)); fax and portal receipt dates count (MCPM 29 sec. 310.2); weekend/holiday deadlines roll forward. The WPS manual states portal appeals after 4:30 PM CT count as the next business day (stated in its Part A appeal guidance).
Routing: file with the contractor named on the RA (405.944(a)). Railroad Retirement beneficiaries' Part B claims are processed by Palmetto GBA, not CGS/WPS (MCPM Ch. 1 sec. 10.1.6).

Telephone reopenings: MCPM Ch. 34 sec. 10.5 makes them 'Required for A/B MACs (B)' for minor errors (not medical necessity or document review); the CGS and WPS pages read point providers to the portals and did not describe phone procedures.

Interest has no request channel: the MAC computes clean-claim interest and reports it per claim on the remittance (MCPM Ch. 1 sec. 80.2.2); a missing-interest question goes in a written inquiry (45 business days).
does_not_apply: Kentucky and Indiana prompt-pay laws, insurance-department complaints, bad-faith remedies and ERISA do not govern a Medicare Administrative Contractor; Part B payment timing and interest come only from SSA 1842(c) and 42 CFR 405.922, and appeal remedies only from SSA 1869 / 42 CFR 405 Subpart I.
No interest, deemed approval or escalation when the MAC misses the 60-day redetermination deadline; a QIC dismisses a reconsideration filed before a redetermination exists (42 CFR 405.972(b)(6)).
No clean-claim interest on full denials or on denied claims paid later on appeal (MCPM Ch. 1 secs. 80.2.2 and 80.2.2.1(C)); clean-claim interest covers only clean claims paid after day 30.

31 USC 3902's other provisions (e.g., its penalty rules in subsection (c)) are not imported: SSA 1842(c)(2)(C) borrows only 'the rate used for purposes of section 3902(a)' (reading of the statute text).
Reopening is discretionary; refusal to reopen is not appealable (42 CFR 405.980(a)(5), 405.926(l)); a reopening request does not stop the 120-day appeal clock (MCPM Ch. 34 sec. 10).

The Physician Fee Schedule rate itself and its components cannot be appealed (42 CFR 405.926(c); MCPM Ch. 29 sec. 200.C(3) NOTE); only the payment amount applied to a specific claim line is appealable.

Timely-filing denials have no formal appeal (42 CFR 405.926(n); MCPM Ch. 1 sec. 70.6 allows only informal review); claims more than 1 calendar year after the date of service are barred except under 424.44(b).

Rejected/unprocessable claims (incomplete or invalid data) have no appeal rights and cannot be reopened; correct and resubmit within timely filing (42 CFR 405.926(s); MCPM Ch. 1 sec. 80.3.2; WPS portal manual).
Third-party (other payer) error is neither a clerical error nor good cause for reopening (42 CFR 405.980(c)(3), 405.986(c)).
Clerical reopenings cannot add services that were never billed (MCPM Ch. 34 sec. 10.4).
Medicare sequestration reductions (CARC 253, up to 2% per 2 USC 901a(6)(A), ordered for FY2022-2031) are statutory, not underpayments.
Failure of a billing company, vendor or software to file on time is not good cause for a late appeal (MCPM Ch. 29 sec. 240.3).
Non-participating physicians on unassigned claims are not parties except for 1842(l) refund situations or as the beneficiary's appointed representative (42 CFR 405.906(b)(4); CGS level-1 page).
There is no CMS form or procedure for a provider to 'claim' 1842(c) interest; it is automatic.

CGS J15 Part B does not accept faxed redeterminations (CGS job aid rev. 12/16/2025: 'Redeterminations do not accept faxed request.'); CGS lists no fax channel for written reopenings either (its reopening forms and addresses page give mail only).
open_questions: WPS J8 Indiana fax number for redeterminations/clerical reopenings: (608) 224-3502 on the J8 Part B Redetermination Request Form (02/19/26) vs (608) 224-3504 on the J8 Part B Redetermination of an Overpayment Request Form (02/18/2026). WPS's 'How to Appeal a Claim Determination' guide and its fax cover sheet page are a JavaScript app I could not read. Confirm with WPS before automating faxes.

Whether WPS accepts several ICNs or beneficiaries on one faxed redetermination form (the form has one beneficiary block and an ICN table); a search-engine summary claimed 'each claim or ICN needs its own form' but I could not read the source page.
Whether CGS and WPS currently run telephone reopenings (MCPM Ch. 34 sec. 10.5 requires A/B MACs (B) to offer them); not described on the pages read.

No CMS instruction found on how a provider recovers missing 1842(c) interest, or whether an interest omission is itself a reopenable computational error; MCPM says only that interest is reported on the remittance.
Whether a favorable redetermination or reopening counts as 'a written determination of an underpayment' that triggers 42 CFR 405.378 interest if unpaid after 30 days; not stated in the sources read.
Whether clean-claim interest is owed when a claim is paid late after a reopening (MCPM Ch. 1 sec. 80.2.2.1(C) speaks only of appeals).
Current 42 CFR 405.378 rate (higher of the Treasury private consumer rate or current value of funds rate) was not looked up.
Exact 835 segment the MACs use for clean-claim interest was not confirmed from CMS text (MCPM Ch. 1 sec. 80.2.2 says 'on the remittance record').
Where CMS currently publishes MAC performance results under SSA 1874A(b)(3)(A)(iv) was not located.

The CMS QIC map file (qic-maps.ppt, last saved 2022) lists QIC addresses but not states in text; Indiana's assignment to QIC Part B North rests on WPS's 2023 appeal-rights sheet and Kentucky's on CGS's reconsideration form. Always use the QIC named on the MRN.
